instances.spoken_text: Consider a publisher. Raise one hundred and fifty million dollars using seven percent debt or new shares at ten dollars. Existing shares total ninety million. What annual EBIT makes EPS equal under both options, in millions of dollars?

follow_up.question: Why does a common tax rate cancel from this breakeven calculation?
follow_up.reference: If both options have positive taxable income and the same usable tax treatment, the same after-tax multiplier applies to both EPS expressions. Cancelling it leaves the EBIT comparison unchanged.

instances.text: Consider a wholesaler. Raise 300 million dollars using 7 percent debt or new shares at 15 dollars. Existing shares total 90 million. What annual EBIT makes EPS equal under both options, in millions of dollars?
instances.spoken_text: Consider a wholesaler. Raise three hundred million dollars using seven percent debt or new shares at fifteen dollars. Existing shares total ninety million. What annual EBIT makes EPS equal under both options, in millions of dollars?

follow_up.question: What if interest were not tax deductible?
follow_up.reference: With a positive corporate tax rate, debt interest would be paid from after-tax operating profit. The debt option would need a higher EBIT to reach the same EPS crossover.
